source: Historical World Cup penalty shoot-outs (1982-2022), compiled and cross-checked. West Germany counted as Germany. Current-tournament shootouts are merged from live results on the client.

shootouts.note: First-ever penalty shootout in World Cup history (Seville, 8 July 1982). West Germany fought back from 3-1 down in extra time to 3-3, then won the shootout 5-4.
1-1 after extra time (Guadalajara). Socrates and Julio Cesar missed for Brazil; Platini also missed for France but Luis Fernandez sealed it.
0-0 after extra time; host Mexico eliminated.
1-1 after extra time.
0-0 after extra time; David O'Leary scored the decisive kick in Ireland's first World Cup.
0-0 after extra time; Yugoslavia played most of the match a man down. Maradona had his kick saved, but Goycochea's saves won it for Argentina.
1-1 after extra time; Goycochea's saves knocked out host Italy in Naples (Maradona's club city).
1-1 after extra time; Stuart Pearce and Chris Waddle missed for England (Turin).
1-1 after extra time.
2-2 after extra time.
First World Cup Final ever decided by a shootout; 0-0 after extra time. Roberto Baggio skied the decisive miss over the bar; Brazil's 4th title (Pasadena).
2-2 after extra time; Paul Ince and David Batty missed for England; David Beckham had earlier been sent off (Saint-Etienne).
0-0 after extra time; host France advanced en route to the title (Saint-Denis).
1-1 after extra time; Cocu and Ronald de Boer missed for the Netherlands (Marseille).
1-1 after extra time.
0-0 after extra time; co-hosts South Korea reached the semi-finals (Gwangju).
0-0 after extra time; Switzerland were eliminated without conceding a goal in open play across the tournament and failed to score any of their shootout penalties.
1-1 after extra time; host Germany's Jens Lehmann saved two kicks (Berlin).
0-0 after extra time; Lampard, Gerrard and Carragher all missed for England; Ricardo saved three (Gelsenkirchen).
1-1 after extra time; Zidane sent off in extra time for headbutting Materazzi; Trezeguet missed for France; Italy's 4th title (Berlin).
0-0 after extra time; Yuichi Komano missed for Japan; Paraguay reached their first-ever quarter-final (Pretoria).
1-1 after extra time; Luis Suarez's deliberate goal-line handball (red card) and Asamoah Gyan's missed last-minute penalty off the bar preceded the shootout (Johannesburg).
1-1 after extra time; host Brazil advanced, Julio Cesar saving two and Gonzalo Jara hitting the post with the decisive miss (Belo Horizonte).
1-1 after extra time; Keylor Navas starred as Costa Rica reached their first-ever quarter-final.
0-0 after extra time; Louis van Gaal brought on Tim Krul specifically for the shootout, and he saved two kicks.
0-0 after extra time; Sergio Romero saved two to send Argentina to the final; the Netherlands could not use a keeper substitution this time (Sao Paulo).
1-1 after extra time; host Russia's Igor Akinfeev saved two to eliminate Spain (Moscow).
1-1 after extra time; both goalkeepers (Subasic and Schmeichel) saved multiple kicks.
1-1 after extra time; England's first-ever World Cup shootout win, ending a run of previous shootout defeats (Moscow).
2-2 after extra time; Croatia's second shootout win of the tournament, eliminating host Russia (Sochi).
1-1 after extra time; Dominik Livakovic saved three of Japan's kicks.
0-0 after extra time; Spain failed to score any of their three penalties; Morocco reached their first-ever quarter-final en route to a historic semi-final.
1-1 after extra time (Brazil led via Neymar in ET before Petkovic equalised); Livakovic again decisive; Rodrygo and Marquinhos missed for Brazil.
2-2 after extra time (Weghorst equalised in stoppage time); Emiliano Martinez saved two Dutch kicks.

Third World Cup Final decided on penalties (after 1994 and 2006); 3-3 after extra time in a Messi/Mbappe classic (Mbappe hat-trick); Coman and Tchouameni missed for France; Argentina's 3rd title, first since 1986 (Lusail).
